title: papaver rhoeas var. trifidum
intro: Papaver rhoeas var. trifidum, commonly known as the 'Wild Poppy' or 'Red Poppy', is a variant of the common red poppy, characterized by its trifid (three-parted) capsule. This plant has been used in traditional medicine for its potential health benefits, including relief from anxiety, insomnia, and restlessness, as well as its analgesic and sedative effects. The bioactive constituents responsible for its therapeutic actions include alkaloids, such as papaverine and noscapine, which are known for their vasodilatory, antispasmodic, and antitussive properties. However, it is essential to note that Papaver rhoeas var. trifidum contains opium alkaloids, which can be toxic in large doses, making it crucial to use this plant under the guidance of a medical professional.
